findings.element: .b-plan / .b-measure on owner-flight, after the last future moment is deleted
findings.problem: Delete the seventh moment and the right half of the owner's desk becomes one vertical hairline in an empty field. Three things fail at once. .b-measure keeps height:1514px - the whole day span - with nothing standing on it. .b-plan keeps the scrollTop it was holding (937px, measured after deleting seven in a row), and because the content it was scrolled to no longer exists, the 'days away' head, 'Today, 16 July' and 'Behind you, 3 moments' are all above the pane's top edge; the owner is parked in the middle of 1500px of nothing. And nothing in the region says it is empty. Meanwhile the rail still reads 'Nothing is planned until 3 October.', a sentence that promises something on a day that now holds nothing at all. A project that has never had a moment gets a written first move - 'Nothing sits between today and the day yet. Everything you add is measured from it.' - and it is excellent. The same emptiness reached by deleting says nothing. This is the state after the last item is removed, and it is the first place a founder reaches the moment they demo the delete.
findings.fix: When .b-measure renders zero items: (1) set .b-plan.scrollTop = 0 in the same frame as the repaint, since any non-zero offset now shows nothing; (2) size .b-measure to its content instead of daysToDay x pixelsPerDay, so the pane stops scrolling; (3) render, under the 'days away' head, the same single instruction the new project gets, worded for this route - 'Nothing is on the plan. Anything you add appears here, measured from the day.' Separately, in the rail, swap the gap note to 'Nothing is planned yet.' whenever the count of future moments is zero, so the sentence stops naming a date it no longer describes.

findings.element: .b-away and .b-tick on every row of the measure
findings.problem: Round 9 records that the row box is no longer a pointer target and that 'the count, the tick and the words inside it are'. Half of that did not land. .b-grab::after is inset:0 on .b-copy, which is the words block only. elementFromPoint at the centre of .b-away returns the span, its cursor stays 'auto', and a click leaves every .b-grab at aria-expanded=false with focus on the body - the press is simply eaten. The tick behaves the same. But hovering either of them DOES paint the row's plate: .b-copy goes to rgba(255,255,255,0.04), because the hover rule hangs off .b-item and the count is an absolutely positioned child sitting 124px outside it. So the leftmost strip of every row lights the row up under the cursor, in a highlight that does not even contain the thing being hovered, and then refuses the press. On this measure the number is the object - proportional distance is the whole direction - and it is the one part of the row that does not answer. The behaviour gate cannot see it: 'every control does something' iterates buttons, and these are spans.
findings.fix: Move .b-grab::after off .b-copy and position it against .b-item with inset: 0 0 0 calc(-1 * var(--away-lane)), so one hit area covers the count lane, the tick and the words. For [data-stack="follow"] rows offset its top by var(--push) so the expanded area is clipped to the row's own band and never reaches into the row above. Set cursor:pointer and pointer-events:none on .b-away and .b-tick so the button owns the whole strip, and extend the hover plate to that same box so what lights up is what will answer.

findings.problem: One press of '+7' mutates both regions in the same frame - measured with a MutationObserver over every live region - so a screen reader queues two polite announcements of one event in two grammars: 'Saturday 15 August 2026, in 30 days' and 'Send the invitations moved 7 days later.' Walking a moment four days with '+1' produces eight. Worse, role=status sits on .b-undo, the bar that wraps the Undo button and its <kbd>Ctrl Z</kbd>, so the region's text is 'Send the invitations moved 7 days later.UndoCtrl Z' and every announcement ends by reading the keycap aloud - on every move, rename, hide and delete. The stepper is the surface's most repeated gesture; a blind owner nudging a moment three days hears the shortcut recited three times and the useful sentence twice.
findings.fix: Add aria-live="off" to .b-undoAct and to the <kbd> inside .b-undo. Per ARIA a descendant's aria-live governs its own subtree, so the bar keeps role=status on .b-undo itself (which the gate asserts) while announcing only .b-undoText. Then remove role="status" from .b-stepRead and leave it purely as the aria-describedby target the date field already points at, so a move is announced once, by the sentence that names what changed, and the readout is still read when the keyboard arrives on the field.

findings.problem: On a phone the loading frame is vertically centred in the room: .b-who at y=264, the count slab at 301, the today rule at 516. The plan it stands in for starts on the top margin: .b-who at y=28, the rule at 280, with 1692px of page below. The skeleton's internal proportions are exactly right - who-to-count is +37 in both, who-to-rule is +252 in both - which makes the fault worse, not better, because every object it drew is in the correct relationship and the whole block is 236px too low. The instant the data lands, the name and the count the guest was already reading jump a third of a screen upward. The gate's 'nothing hops when the data lands' compares only the relative offset between .b-who and .b-todayLabel, so this translation is invisible to it. This is the flagship second: someone opening the link once, on a phone, while doing something else.
findings.fix: Exempt loading and loading-slow from the centre-in-the-room rule below the two-column breakpoint and stand them on the page's own top margin - the same var(--gap-section) the arrived plan opens on - so .b-who renders at the y it will keep and the arrival changes only slabs into words. Keep the centred treatment for ended, unfurl and day, whose objects genuinely fit the room.

findings.element: the Try again button on loading-slow
findings.problem: Press it and the surface answers well - the heading swaps to 'Bringing in what is ahead.', the region takes aria-busy=true, the reassurance clears - but the control itself is untouched: still enabled, still reading 'Try again', no pressed or working treatment, for the roughly two seconds the retry is in flight. A second press inside that window is absorbed with nothing on the face of the control to show it landed. This is the only control on the guest's stalled screen, the person pressing it is already anxious, and it is the one element on the screen that does not change when they press it. Copy already sets the standard here by answering with 'Copied' on its own face.
findings.fix: While the region is busy, set disabled on the retry control and swap its label to 'Trying...'; restore 'Try again' and remove disabled when aria-busy returns to false. Same mechanism, same duration token, as the copy control's answer.

biggestWin: The keyboard model is complete and it keeps place, which is the hardest thing on this list to fake. Enter on a row opens the editor and names it; Escape closes it and returns focus to the row that opened it; Ctrl Z is real, restores the item, and puts focus back on the stepper that made the change; deleting seven moments one after another never once drops focus to the body - it walks forward to the next row, and when the last one goes, to Add a moment. Every focused control is scrolled into view inside its own pane at 1440, 1280 and 1279 without the window moving, and the 44px floor arrives properly under a coarse pointer on every control including the row's Edit. Forced colours are mapped rather than merely survived: the rail draws as CanvasText, the today rule and the lead tick take Highlight, and the filled next-thing mark stays distinguishable from the hollow ones. Fourteen states, six widths, touch and forced-colours regimes, and not one page error. The first-run sequence - one question, then 'The day is set. Moments come next.' with Add a moment focused and nothing else on the screen to press - is the best-judged moment in the whole artifact.
